25-ji-code-de/nightcord.description: A real-time chat application with a modern, modular architecture. Enjoy Nightcord!
25-ji-code-de/nightcord.body:
# Nightcord

A real-time chat application with a modern, modular architecture.

## ✨ Features

- 🎯 **Highly decoupled** - UI, business logic, and network communication are fully separated
- 📡 **Event-driven** - Uses a publish-subscribe pattern for communication between components
- 🔄 **Auto-reconnect** - WebSocket automatically reconnects after disconnection
- 🧩 **Extensible** - Easily add new features through a plugin system
- 📦 **Modular** - ES6 modules, each class is a separate file
- 🧪 **Easy to test** - Single responsibility, easy to unit test
- 📝 **Complete documentation** - API docs, architecture docs, example docs
- 🤖 **AI integration** - Built-in Nako AI assistant with streaming conversation support
- 🔐 **SSO authentication** - Integrates SEKAI Pass single sign-on
- 📊 **Data reporting** - Automatically reports user activity to SEKAI Platform

### @ Mentions

Type `@` in the input box or click the `@` button to select a member, `everyone`, or AI.
Member mentions are bound to user ID. Users with the same name are listed separately, and mentions still work after a rename. Click a member mention in a message to view their profile.
`@everyone` notifies all recipients in the current room. Personal mentions and everyone mentions both highlight the message and show an in-site notification that can jump to the message.
History playback, duplicate messages, and your own messages do not trigger notifications.

After selecting Nako, Asagi, Miku, or Yukawa Yui, type a question and send it to call the corresponding AI. Click an AI mention in a message to continue asking in the input box.
Each send calls one AI; received messages do not call it again. Existing forms like `@Nako` and `/nako` still work.
The `role` type retains rendering support, awaiting the custom role group feature, and will not trigger group notifications.

### Emoji

Type `::` to open the emoji picker, or type a name like `:joy:`. Unicode emoji typed or pasted directly
use the same emoji images for display, e.g. `😂` and `:joy:` display identically. When copying messages, the original input text is preserved,
so a typed `😂` remains `😂` after copying. Combinations or skin-tone variants not yet in the emoji library are kept as-is.

The Unicode mapping is generated by `scripts/generate-emoji-unicode.mjs`. After updating the emoji library, download
[Unicode Emoji 17.0 data](https://unicode.org/Public/17.0.0/emoji/emoji-test.txt),
and run `node scripts/generate-emoji-unicode.mjs <path to emoji-test.txt>` to update the mapping.

## 📁 Project Structure

```
.
├── event-bus.js              # event bus
├── websocket-mgr.js          #…
```

2670961598/studio.description: Virtual software studio framework (YouTrack + daemon-based scheduling)
2670961598/studio.body:
# Studio Next

Studio Next is a runtime framework for AI Agent organizations.

It models "a company" as a version-controlled company directory, with a resident daemon responsible for scheduling, dispatching, executing, acceptance, and bookkeeping. Execution bodies (DSH, Claude Code, Codex, Kimi, etc.) are replaceable, while organization, processes, and records are persistent assets.

> Current status: The V2 specification was finalized on 2026-10-30 (tag `v2-final`). The core framework has entered the productization wrap-up stage. The V2 finalized baseline is 106 test files and 1583 test cases, all passing. Real-world runtime validation, security hardening, and platform adaptation are still in progress.

## Contents

- [What problem it solves](#它解决什么问题)
- [Core design](#核心设计)
- [Architecture](#架构)
- [Key capabilities](#关键能力)
- [Repository structure](#仓库结构)
- [Quick start](#快速开始)
- [Verification](#验证)
- [Current status and boundaries](#当前状态与边界)
- [Documentation](#文档)
- [Project history](#项目沿革)
- [Contributing](#贡献)
- [License](#license)
- [Contact](#联系)

## What problem it solves

A single Agent can complete one task, but it is hard for it to independently carry a continuously running business chain. A real company needs more than a "smarter executor." It also needs:

- who has the authority to initiate, who is responsible for execution, and who accepts;
- how tasks are decomposed, dispatched, resumed, and recovered;
- how outputs are recorded as evidence, audited, and rolled back;
- how costs, permissions, concurrency, and failures are handled;
- how organizational knowledge is retained when personnel or execution bodies are replaced.

Studio Next turns these from "prompt conventions" into runnable, inspectable mechanisms. The company directory carries organization and rules, the ledger carries facts and accounts, the daemon carries operation, and execution bodies only execute.

## Core design

1. **The company is a directory**
   A company is a git directory: `org-config.yaml` defines the organization, `charter.md` defines the charter and red lines, `departments/` stores department and personnel files, `reports/` stores outputs, and `.AIWS/` stores employee workspaces. Organization and rules can be reviewed, migrated, and rolled back.

2. **Three sources of fact, each with a single writer**
   - Collaboration platform: written only through the framework gateway;
   - Company git directory: the daemon is the sole writer;
   - SQLite ledger: written by the daemon; it is a rebuildable projection.

3. **Execution bodies are replaceable**
   DSH (DeepSeek Harness) is the default execution body, and it also adapts to Claude Code, Codex, Kimi, etc. Execution bodies are labor; organization and processes are the persistent assets.

4. **Delivery relies on process and evidence, not on "not making mistakes"**
   Tasks form a complete chain from ticket creation, dispatch, execution, and acceptance through re-verification and merge. Acceptance commands are actually run, and key results are recorded in the ledger. Failures must be explicitly classified; silent degradation is not allowed.

Configure within the card, install with a single command, register automatically, and it's ready to use once installed.
Lbunc/dsh-local-llm-controller.body:
# dsh-local-llm-controller

**DSH plugin: one-click start/stop of a local llama.cpp server on the Settings page, making local large models usable as DSH session models**

Configuration card location: Settings → Plugins → Local LLM Controller

[English](https://github.com/Lbunc/dsh-local-llm-controller/blob/HEAD/README.en.md) | **Simplified Chinese**

***

> **Compatibility note**: DSH 0.1.7-rc.1 underwent a major low-level refactor. Since v2.1.0, this plugin has been adapted to that architecture (adapted for the RC branch only; other branches are not guaranteed).

## Features

- **One-click start/stop of the local service**: Start or stop llama-server from the Settings → Plugins card. Status, error reasons, and recent logs are shown on the same card. When DSH restarts, the plugin automatically cleans up child processes.
- **Dual-slot model management**: Slots A and B each bind to a model folder and automatically scan all GGUF files in it to generate a candidate list. Vision projectors (mmproj) are detected automatically, and vision mode mounts automatically.
- **Eight sets of startup parameters**: Divided by slot × text/vision × fast/long-context. Parameter rows can be freely added or removed, base parameters are prefilled, and each row can be marked as a switch or a value.
- **One-click session integration**: Writes the selected model to DSH's Models page, so the local model can be selected at the bottom of a session for chatting.
- **Local compression engine** (v2.1.2): Provides a local alternative to DSH's built-in compression engine as a subpath export, targeting local windows of 32k\~256k. See “Local compression engine” below.

> This plugin only handles the connection and control between DSH and llama.cpp. It does not include the llama-server binary itself, and it does not handle model downloads. These come from upstream [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) and community quantized releases (such as Hugging Face), respectively.

## Quick Start

### Installation

Installing through DSH's built-in plugin manager is recommended: in the sidebar, go to Settings → Plugins → Add plugin, enter any of the addresses in the table below, choose an install source, then install and enable. No restart of DSH Web is required after installation.

You can also install from the command line (running the same command again upgrades; if already on the latest version, it prints `Already up to date`):

```text
dsh plugin --profile web add <地址>
```

| Address form             | Description                                                 |
| :----------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------- |
| dsh-local-llm-controller | Package name; installs the latest published release from the npm registry |
| Local folder path…       |

## iOS App Maintenance

Free Apple ID signing typically expires after 7 days. When the app won't open after expiration, reconnect the iPhone and press `Cmd + R` in Xcode to reinstall and renew the signing for 7 more days:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22
npx cap open ios
```

If you're only renewing the signing without changing content, you don't need to rebuild the web artifacts.

If you've modified the blog content, you need to rebuild and sync first:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 16.19.1
MOBILE=1 npm run docs:build

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22.22.2
npx cap sync ios
npx cap open ios
```

Then select iPhone in Xcode and press `Cmd + R` to install.

Nefelibata857/resume-autofill.body:
# Resume Autofill Helper · Resume Autofill

> Enter your resume information once; afterwards, click a browser bookmark on any corporate online application page and the entire form fills in automatically.

**Use online (no download or installation required)**: <https://nefelibata857.github.io/resume-autofill/>

---

## Three ways to use it, pick what fits

| What you want | How |
|---|---|
| **Use online** (recommended, up and running in one minute) | Open the URL above, enter your information → click 'Install form-fill bookmark' → press Ctrl+D to save it as a bookmark |
| **Download and use locally** (don't want to rely on the website / want offline use) | [Click here to download the whole project](https://github.com/Nefelibata857/resume-autofill/archive/refs/heads/main.zip), unzip, then double-click `index.html` |
| **Customize** (adapt to your industry and your fields) | Fork the repository or download and modify `index.html`; see the [modification guide](https://github.com/Nefelibata857/resume-autofill/blob/HEAD/修改指南.md) |

> The downloaded version has full functionality: resume recognition, bookmark generation, and data self-check all work.
> The only difference is that 'PDF recognition' requires the `vendor/` folder in the same directory (it is included if you download everything together), so don't copy `index.html` on its own.

---

## What problem it solves

The most time-consuming part of campus recruitment applications isn't the submission itself, but typing over and over, across dozens of different websites, your name, phone number, ID number, school, major, GPA, ranking, three internship experiences... Beisen, Moka, and enterprise-built recruiting backends each order their fields differently, but the content is always the same.

This tool stores this information centrally once, then uses a browser bookmark (bookmarklet) to run a script on any page that automatically identifies fields and fills them in.

**Pure front-end, single file, zero dependencies, no network.** Data is stored only in your own browser's localStorage and is never uploaded to any server.

---

## Features

| Capability | Description |
|---|---|
| **Automatic resume recognition** | Drag a PDF / TXT into the page; it automatically extracts name, phone, email, school, major, GPA, ranking, experience, skills, etc., and writes them only after you preview and confirm each item |
| **Custom fields** | When an application asks questions not covered above (driver's license, willingness to travel on business, height, etc.), add a row yourself, and the bookmark will look for that field name on the page |
| **100 fields managed centrally** | Basic info, education background (1–4 entries: undergraduate / master's / doctoral), job intention, internship experience (2 entries), project experience (6 items), long text (self-evaluation / skills / awards), all visually editable |
| **Internship / project matched separately** | …

chen1111-a/hkid-quota-monitor.body:
# Hong Kong ID Card Appointment Quota Dashboard

Monitors smart ID card appointment quotas at the six Registration of Persons Offices of the Hong Kong Immigration Department, checking about every 2 minutes, and alerts subscribers via email / Feishu group when slots are released. **A third-party public-interest tool, not an official Immigration Department service. It only monitors and sends alerts, and does not grab or book appointments on anyone's behalf.**

## Dashboard entry

- **Preferred (stable direct access from mainland China):** https://hkid-quota-monitor.pages.dev/
- Backup: https://chen1111-a.github.io/hkid-quota-monitor/
  (github.io is intermittently unreachable from mainland networks; jsDelivr/raw direct links carry a nosniff header and only display source code, so do not use them as web entry points)
- The full experience in mainland China without a VPN is through **email subscription + Feishu group**. The notification path is entirely domestic and direct, so slot releases are pushed to your phone immediately. The dashboard is only a supplement.

## How it works

```
cron-job.org (every 2 minutes) ──▶ GitHub Actions
                            │  python -m quota_monitor.run
                            │  ├─ fetch the Immigration Department's public quota API (read-only, one request per run)
                            │  ├─ diff against previous snapshot → slot-release events
                            │  └─ commit data/ + refresh jsDelivr cache
                            ▼
        index.html dashboard (mobile-first, auto-refresh every 90 seconds)
        Email + Feishu notifications (triggered by slot-release events, with debounce cooldown)
```

- API structure: [docs/api-notes.md](https://github.com/chen1111-a/hkid-quota-monitor/blob/HEAD/docs/api-notes.md)
- 2-minute trigger configuration: [docs/cron-setup.md](https://github.com/chen1111-a/hkid-quota-monitor/blob/HEAD/docs/cron-setup.md)

## Improvements over similar tools

- **Mobile-first:** dates scroll vertically in rows, so all six offices fit on one screen without horizontal table scrolling
- **Colorblind-friendly:** status cells use both color and text (available / low / full)
- **Prevents notification flooding:** the official API has load-balancing data jitter (measured 304↔346 cell fluctuation within the same minute), so the notification layer has a per-cell cooldown and does not alert on every cycle
- **Direct mainland access:** email subscription and Feishu notifications are reachable domestically without needing to circumvent internet restrictions

# denpa

The documentation is also available at **[danything.github.io/denpa](https://danything.github.io/denpa/)**.

**A home TV recording server that works out of the box as soon as you plug in a tuner.**
No configuration file is needed. The tuner type (terrestrial / satellite) is detected automatically, and you just press scan on the screen.
You don't need Mirakurun, EDCB, or a media server. Reserve programs from the program guide, commercials are skipped automatically,
and you can watch both live and recorded content in the browser with subtitles and data broadcasting. For TV, use the dedicated app
[denpa-tv](https://github.com/danything/denpa-tv).

If you're upgrading from 1.x, first read [What changed in 2.0](https://github.com/danything/denpa/blob/HEAD/docs/v2.md) (screen locations and removed settings).

denpa is meant only for recording and watching **with your own B-CAS card, within your own household, privately**.

- Don't show recordings or live streams to people outside your household
- Don't distribute the card's keys to devices outside your household
- Don't rewrite the card

The only thing the client (browser) connects to directly on external services is live commentary, and only when it is turned on in settings. It connects to NX-Jikkyo and the Niconico Jikkyo past-log API, and those services can see the client's IP address and which channel is being watched and when ([docs/architecture.md](https://github.com/danything/denpa/blob/HEAD/docs/architecture.md#端末が外へ繋ぐもの-実況のコメント)).
When watching live, you can post to NX-Jikkyo. What you post is made public and cannot be deleted ([docs/watch.md](https://github.com/danything/denpa/blob/HEAD/docs/watch.md#実況に書き込む)).

The reasoning behind this is summarized in [Discussion #760](https://github.com/danything/denpa/discussions/760). It is not legal advice; it is an organized basis for discussion.

# nfqws2-android

Full-featured port of **nfqws2** ([zapret2](https://github.com/bol-van/zapret) by bol-van) with support for Keenetic strategy syntax on Android.

Write down ideas, see their structure.

# Femiwiki MediaWiki Server

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> This docker image is specifically designed for the needs of FemiWiki, contains
> FemiWiki-specific configurations and includes arbitrary MediaWiki extensions.
> It is not recommended to use this image for general purposes. We recommend
> using the
> [Docker official image for MediaWiki](https://hub.docker.com/_/mediawiki/).

This is the MediaWiki Docker image used for [femiwiki.com], a feminist wiki in Korea.
It contains various code, including the Dockerfile and a Docker Compose file for testing.

## Usage of Docker Image

This is a [PHP-FPM] server for Femiwiki, and the same image can also be used to run the [Caddy] web server. Please refer to the example Compose file below. You can see a full development example that can be run in compose.yaml.

```yml
fastcgi:
  image: ghcr.io/femiwiki/femiwiki
http:
  image: ghcr.io/femiwiki/femiwiki
  command: caddy run
  ports:
    - 80:80
  volumes:
    - ./path/to/Caddyfile:/srv/femiwiki.com/Caddyfile:ro
```

### MediaWiki

The following environment variables can be set.

- `MEDIAWIKI_SERVER`: Overrides `$wgServer`. Default `'https://femiwiki.com'`.
- `MEDIAWIKI_DEBUG_MODE`: If set, enables the debug features provided by MediaWiki and disables extensions that are difficult to configure in a development environment.
- `MEDIAWIKI_SKIP_INSTALL`: If set, install.php is not run when the container starts. install.php checks whether the database has not been set up and initializes it, and it also generates LocalSettings.php, so it can be skipped when both of these have already been handled…

heqvyfrogg/silentbox.body:
# tbx — Unofficial native client for TeraBox

A TeraBox client with no ads, parallel transfers, and drive mounting. Written in Rust, it provides a CLI, a TUI, and OS-native mounting from the same core.

This is a separate implementation that ports the protocol by analyzing the official app (`com.dubox.drive` 4.28.2). It does not modify or redistribute the APK. The basis for the analysis is in `docs/protocol.md`.

## Features

- **Zero ads.** The official app bundles ad SDKs from 8 networks (Pangle, Moloco, Mintegral, Smaato, Vungle, AppLovin, InMobi, Facebook). This client includes none of them.
- **Parallel downloads.** Splits downloads using `Range` specifications and resumes from where it left off after an interruption. In measurements, 4 connections performed best (on the free tier, 8 connections were actually slower).
- **Split uploads.** Sends files in parts and skips parts that have already been sent.
- **Bulk folder download.** `tbx get /dir` reproduces the directory hierarchy and downloads everything together.
- **Multiple accounts.** Stored by name and switched with `--account`.
- **Share links.** Resolves `/s/1xxxx`, lists the contents, and saves them to your own space.
- **External player playback.** Passes the dlink to mpv / VLC / ffplay.
- **Capacity and limit visibility.** Displays only values returned by the server and does not fill in guesses. Also shows the free-tier breakdown (permanent + time-limited) and expiration dates.
- **Drive mounting.** WinFsp on Windows, FUSE on Linux / macOS, and WebDAV everywhere.
- **TUI.** Handles listing, transfers, sharing, and capacity on one screen.

## Requirements

| Purpose | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Build | Rust 1.90 or later | Measured with 1.96.0 (Windows). Dependencies do not resolve on 1.82 |
| Login | Chrome-based browser | Must be able to speak CDP. Firefox does not work |
| Mounting on Windows | WinFsp 2.x | Without it, WebDAV mode still works |
| Building on Windows | MSVC target | `winfsp-sys` fails with `windows-gnu` |
| Mounting on Linux | `fuse3` (`fusermount3`) and `/dev/fuse` | Kernel-side FUSE is also required |

# Sub2Aouter Apophis Theme

**A sustainably updatable, customized front-end distribution based on Sub2API**

Apophis-style home page, authentication pages, user console, and admin dashboard. Retains Sub2API's original backend, database, APIs, authentication, and business features.

## Project Positioning

This repository does not reimplement Sub2API and does not modify its business protocols. Instead, it maintains a repeatably applicable front-end theme layer on top of the official upstream source code:

```text
Wei-Shaw/sub2api upstream source
            │
            ▼
Apply theme/apophis overlay
            │
            ▼
Frontend/backend tests + Docker build
            │
      ┌─────┴─────┐
      ▼           ▼
themed-release   GHCR image
```

- `main`: permanent theme, overlay scripts, workflows, and release configuration.
- `themed-release`: deployable source code automatically generated from the latest upstream.
- `ghcr.io/kibght/sub2aouter:latest`: latest themed image, published after tests pass.

- Black-and-white grid background and floating navigation.

# IOTA Watch

An open-source, five-language, multi-project monitoring dashboard centered on **IOTA Train at Home**. It supports IOTA, XID / MMM, Quantus, fly.ai, Nosana, Gonka, Akash, io.net, Vast.ai and Golem; each project's inputs, cycles, and data coverage are described separately.

**[Official site](https://iotahome.site) · [My Devices](https://iotahome.site/zh/devices) · [IOTA Lookup](https://iotahome.site/zh/app) · [Network Status](https://iotahome.site/zh/network) · [Blog](https://iotahome.site/zh/blog) · [English](https://iotahome.site/en)**

IOTA Watch is an independent MIT-licensed monitor in English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Korean and Japanese. IOTA Train at Home (Macrocosmos / Bittensor SN9) is the core project, with ten project pages covering training, mining and compute. Tool pages query records; separate tutorials explain identifiers, fields and troubleshooting. Public projects use public identifiers; io.net and Vast.ai require account connections with read credentials. Those two integrations have mocked validation; real-account validation remains pending.

The screenshot shows miner distribution and network capacity; the figures are official data as of when the screenshot was taken.

## Features

- **Multi-device monitoring**: add, name, and view devices by public Miner ID, filtering by contributing, waiting for tasks, needs checking, and pending confirmation.
- **Earnings records**: today, cumulative, paid, pending payment, frozen, and minimum payment amounts; also shows USD valuations with source and timestamp.
- **Training history**: view training tokens, throughput, and cumulative tokens by day, week, or month; missing data is left as gaps.
- **Network visualization**: regional distribution donut chart, miner count rankings, slot occupancy, task progress, and tier overview.
-…

nowscott/EverydayTechNews.body:
# EverydayTechNews (Daily Tech News)

Automatically sends tech news to your email every morning.

Click [here](https://mailist.nowscott.top/) to subscribe to the daily tech morning briefing.

[action-url]: https://github.com/NowScott/EverydayTechNews/actions/workflows/run-selenium-script.yml "Action State"
[action-image]:https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/nowscott/EverydayTechNews/run-selenium-script.yml?label=新闻抓取
[forks-url]:https://github.com/NowScott/EverydayTechNews/forks
[forks-image]:https://img.shields.io/github/forks/NowScott/EverydayTechNews?label=Forks

## Origin

When I was young, the elders in my family often subscribed to newspapers. However, as times changed, newspapers gradually disappeared from our view, replaced by the ubiquitous internet news.

In this vast ocean of information, content is abundant yet chaotic, containing a great deal of information. In reality, though, I don't care about many of the topics.

Therefore, I created this tool to automatically send tech news to my email every day.

This way, I no longer drown in a flood of information, but like when reading newspapers in the past, I can focus only on the parts I'm most interested in.

## Tool Introduction

Because I don't want to expose my personal email, the tool that actually runs daily lives in another private repository. The purpose of this project is to help friends with the same need build such a small tool.

This small tool for automatically sending news to email is developed in Python. The email entry point is `src/main.py`, and notification copy configuration is located in the root directory's `notifications.ini`.

### Code Structure

- `src/script.py`: Scrapes news using Requests + BeautifulSoup and writes it to the archive
- `src/news_sorter.py`: Concurrently requests the IT之家 rating API and sorts
- `src/news_filter.py`: Unified filtering rules for ads, prices, and topic keywords
- `src/newsletter.py`: Selects news and generates email HTML
- `src/notion_client.py`: Reads subscribers and updates subscription status
- `src/subscription_links.py`: Generates signed unsubscribe links for the daily email
- `src/mailer.py`: SMTP connection reuse, reconnection on disconnect, retries, and failure classification
- `src/main.py`: Loads configuration and orchestrates the daily email task

soulmachine/ubuntu-provision.body:
# Ubuntu Provision

Uses Ansible to automate **Ubuntu** development environment setup: system software is installed via **apt**, language runtimes are handled by mise, and other tools follow their own official `curl | sh` install scripts plus `npm` / `bun` / `uv` global packages. The shell is Ubuntu's built-in **bash**, configured with starship, zoxide, fzf, and Omarchy's shell environment.

This repository is the Ubuntu port of the sibling `macbook-provision` (macOS version), targeting **Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (amd64)**, serving the supermicro and grok-bot machines. The correspondence with upstream (synced commit, intentionally omitted roles) is recorded in the "Upstream" section of `AGENTS.md`, and every intentional difference is recorded in `DECISIONS.md`.

## Language Runtimes

This project uses [mise](https://github.com/jdx/mise) to install language runtimes (Go, Node.js, JDK, etc.) instead of the system package manager. mise is a multi-language version manager that supports installing and switching between multiple versions on the same machine, for example switching freely between JDK 22 and JDK 23. mise is cross-platform, so this part is fully identical to the macOS version. Python is the exception: it is managed by uv (`bootstrap.sh` installs 3.14 and does not override the system `python3`).

## Usage

### 1. Install Ansible

```bash
./bootstrap.sh
```

This script configures passwordless sudo, installs apt base dependencies (`build-essential`, `curl`, `git`, `python3` / `python3-apt`, etc.), uv and Python 3.14, mise, and finally installs Ansible with `uv tool install --with ansible ansible-core`. It also adds `~/.local/bin` and mise's shims directory to `~/.bashrc` **above the non-interactive guard** (before `case $- in`), so that non-interactive shells such as `ssh host 'cmd'` can also find them.

> **About passwordless sudo**: Tasks marked `become: true` in Ansible (apt installs, apt repository setup for gh / Docker / Tailscale, etc.) require that `sudo` not show a password prompt when run unattended. The script does this by writing a rule `<用户名> ALL=(ALL)…` to `/etc/sudoers.d/<用户名>-nopasswd`.

yurika0211/lucky-agent.description: LuckyAgent — an Agent framework focused on long-task planning and system memory
yurika0211/lucky-agent.body:
# LuckyAgent

The LuckyAgent main repository maintains the public Agent core library and keeps a thin entry point for building the complete `lh` program. Models, sessions, memory, RAG, and application entry points come from independent Go modules and are assembled to run within the same process.

It is not just a single chat window; it provides an Agent infrastructure that can be observed, configured, and run continuously.

## Interface Preview

## Embed SDK (In-Process)

Embed LuckyAgent as a Go library in a host process without first starting `lh serve`. The SDK lives in `luckyagent-app`, imported as `github.com/yurika0211/luckyagent-app/sdk`.

```go
agent, err := sdk.New(sdk.Config{
    HomeDir:  "/var/lib/myapp/luckyagent",
    Provider: "openai",
    Model:    "gpt-5.4-mini",
    APIKey:   os.Getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"),
})
```

For details, see [luckyagent-app/sdk/README.md](https://github.com/yurika0211/luckyagent-app/blob/main/sdk/README.md). Stable surface (v0): `New` / `Chat*` (including multimodal Input) / Sessions (including Compact) / Memory / RAG / Tools / Models / Skills. The Agent loop itself is `github.com/yurika0211/lucky-agent/agent`; full application assembly goes through the SDK.

## Core Capabilities

- **Unified runtime**: The CLI, HTTP API, and message gateway share the same Agent core.
- **Session storage**: Concurrent saves, backup/restore, and deletion use the same lifecycle protection; cold metadata updates do not load the body, and paginating large histories reuses offset indexes. See [Session storage reliability](https://github.com/yurika0211/lucky-agent/blob/HEAD/docs/session-reliability.md).
- **Session recap**: After each turn completes, the Agent asynchronously generates a one-sentence recap in the same language; the runtime persists it, and Android and the CLI reuse it for display. Requires matching runtime/app versions. See [Generation and display boundaries](https://github.com/yurika0211/lucky-agent/blob/HEAD/docs/session-recap.md).
- **Long-term memory**: Uses an Obsidian-compatible Markdown vault…
